chapters.summary: Majority Leader Abreu introduces Chaplain Patrick Lime of Fort Hamilton; Lime delivers a benediction reflecting on military chaplaincy, religious freedom, and service.
chapters.title: Invocation delivered by Captain Patrick Lime

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now have today's invocation delivered by Captain Patrick Lime, chaplain at Fort Hamilton in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Welcome, Captain Lime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: My name is Chaplain Patrick Lime, but I was not invited here merely because of who I am, but because of the office and calling that I represent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: I serve as the Garrison Chaplain at Fort Hamilton in Brooklyn, providing religious support to the 50,000 service members, family members, retirees throughout the greater New York City metropolitan area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: As a chaplain in the United States Army, my presence conveys the continuity of spiritual care to our service members, representing to our sons and daughters charged with carrying our republic through some of the darkest recesses of human existence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: We represent the force that walks with them, and we bear on our collars and carry in our lives the marks of the religious traditions that speak to courage, grief, duty, mercy, sacrifice, and hope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: We are present when questions of purpose no longer are abstract, when they become immediate, personal, and profound.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: But the military does not exist merely to project power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: It exists to preserve the way of life that's ordered by liberty under law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: Within that mission, the chaplaincy was a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: established not as an optional comfort, but in recognition of the institutions that allow free citizens, even in uniform, to remain free in conscience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: It's for this reason that the chaplain's purpose is twofold and inseparable, to provide for the free exercise of religion by those who share the chaplain's own tradition,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: and to guarantee that every service member, regardless of their tradition, may in like exercise their same liberties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: It's customary in an occasion such as this for a chaplain to offer an invocation to call upon God's presence and blessing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: And while I assure you that God is present amongst us, I think that he came in during the roll call.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: What I would rather do is offer a benediction, a word from Latin, bene, meaning well or good, and diction, meaning to speak, literally to speak a blessing over this body and its service to the people of the Newark City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: And so from my tradition and with respect for all those gathered here, may you receive

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: the peace of God which transcends all understanding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: May your hearts be inclined towards his goodness, justice, and mercy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: May the spirit of wisdom and truth grant you ears to hear and eyes to see that you may both perceive and understand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: May you walk with God humbly, with discernment, and in pursuit of peace and the prosperity of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: I pray these things through Christ our Lord.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Captain Patrick Lime
utterances.text: Amen.

chapters.summary: Morano thanks Chaplain Lime, recounts his military service and family, and moves for unanimous consent to spread the invocation in full upon the record.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano moves to spread invocation and honors Chaplain Lime

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Captain Lime.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now ask Councilmember Frank Marano to spread the invocation on the record.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want to thank Chaplain Patrick Lime for joining us today and for that beautiful invocation.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think it's especially fitting that we have Chaplain Lime with us today, just one day after Veterans Day, and as this council prepares to take up several important pieces of legislation

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: to help the men and women who have served our country and live in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Chaplain Lime knows something about service.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: He enlisted in the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Army at just 17 years old, served as a combat medic, and spent 12 months deployed in Iraq.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But his service didn't end when he came home, as is the case for so many veterans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: He answered another calling, entering the ministry and eventually returning to active duty as an Army chaplain.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And today, he serves as the garrison chaplain at Fort Hamilton right here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Among his many honors is the Four Chaplains Medal, named in memory of four military chaplains who gave their lives helping others aboard a sinking troop ship during World War II.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And it's a powerful reminder that service isn't just about what we're willing to do for others, but sometimes what we're willing to sacrifice for them.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I also want to recognize his beautiful family who have joined us today, his wife Erin and his two children, Emily and Ethan.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And we sometimes forget that when someone serves in our...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: military, the whole family makes sacrifices too.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So thank you for your service and for your sacrifice as well.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as chairman of this council's Veterans Committee, it's a particular honor to welcome someone who's devoted so much of his life to serving both God and country.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Chaplain Lime, thank you for your service.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for your prayers.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for being here on such an important day for our city's veterans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I just wish you could have helped God deliver some better weather.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: With that, I move for unanimous consent to spread the invocation in full upon the record.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin offers condolences for the eight lives lost in a Flatbush building collapse, notes 23 injured including three firefighters, thanks first responders, and leads a moment of silence.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon mourns Flatbush building collapse victims and leads moment of silence

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So today, my colleagues and I joined New Yorkers across the five boroughs in mourning the eight lives that were lost in the tragic...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Collapse of a building in Flatbush.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Councilmember Farrah Lewis represents that community.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Myself and my office has been in constant touch with her.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: She is obviously on the ground responding to her constituents'needs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: All of us here at the council are thinking of the victims, their families, their loved ones, of the pain they must feel and the indelible loss that no words can make up for.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're also thinking of the 23 New Yorkers that are injured, including three brave firefighters, and we are certainly praying for their swift recovery.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we're incredibly grateful for the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: approximately 250 first responders who raced to the scene and who have been working tirelessly throughout the night on this heroic rescue efforts.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I want to begin my remarks today with a moment of silence in the victim's honor.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's times like this which certainly remind us that whenever our city is staring tragedy in the face, New Yorkers have always been able to find solace in each other.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin honors the 265 victims of Flight 587 and the Dominican community in Balharbor, recalling neighbors' immediate support.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon marks 25th anniversary of Flight 587

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we also recognize the 25th anniversary of Flight 587, which devastated the Dominican community and the Balharbor neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We will always remember the 265 people who tragically died that day and how residents immediately came together to honor their lives.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Hundreds of neighbors showed up at the crash site, bringing water and basic necessities on top of their love and condolences.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: In times of grief, we clutch that united resolve and unconquered spirit, but we also carry it with us in the moments where we strive to build a better future as a city, as a state, as a nation.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin thanks New Yorkers and Americans for voting in the midterm elections, saying democracy grows stronger with participation.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon celebrates midterm election participation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On that note, last Tuesday, millions of Americans headed to the polls for the midterm elections.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And of course, quite a few of us here in New York even went and voted early.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our democracy grows so much stronger every single time that we participate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I want to thank our fellow New Yorkers and Americans for that ever-increasing strength.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin highlights Art Week NYC, a citywide contemporary art festival with free events over two days, emphasizing accessibility amid affordability challenges.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon announces Art Week NYC free access

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday marked the start of the inaugural Art Week NYC, which is a citywide festival dedicated to contemporary art.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And for the next two days, New Yorkers all across the city have free access to a truly unparalleled list of events,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: because art should be accessible to anyone and enjoyed by everyone, particularly in the midst of an affordability crisis.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin explains how companies use personal data to set different prices for identical goods, citing a TV price jump and grocery delivery price differences, worsening the affordability crisis.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon describes surveillance pricing's impact on affordability

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: While this crisis shouldn't crush any working class New Yorker, millions of residents are feeling it, the heavy weight of higher costs of gas, of groceries, of health insurance, and so much more.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: There are so many factors that are driving up costs, but some of them are quite obvious to consumers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But a more subtle reason is the insidious and predatory corporate practice of surveillance pricing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Companies are collecting the personal information of New Yorkers and then using it to their detriment.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For different consumers that are shopping at the same time, companies are oftentimes setting different prices on literally the exact same product,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: taking advantage of their demographic, web browsing history, don't ever leave that shopping cart open when you are buying something, shopping habits, and social media activity.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: all to make New Yorkers pay more.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: One investigation found that upon arriving at the parking lot of a department store, the price of a TV jumped $100

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: for one interested shopper who had been browsing online to look for a TV simply because the retailer had access to their location data through their phone and knew that they were about to walk into that store to buy that TV.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another revealed that a major grocery delivery platform was individualizing price differences right here in New York as high as 23% between customers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's a practice that erodes privacy.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's a practice that erodes fairness.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's a practice that worsens the affordability crisis.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin announces the Council will ban surveillance pricing, with fines up to $1,000 per violation, small-business safe harbor, and protections for legitimate discounts.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon details surveillance pricing ban and penalties

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And today, it's a practice that we are going to ban, making us the first jurisdiction in the nation to ban surveillance pricing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Earlier this year, I introduced legislation to prohibit businesses from using the individual data of consumers to set specific prices for them, whether it's tracking their mouse movements or mapping their location.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Feel free to disagree.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He's talking now, but I'm about to make a joke about him.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Feel free to disagree, but Councilmember Harvey Epstein should not need to pay more than his constituents for pet food, even if a retailer knows from his search history that he'd do anything for his dog, Homer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we all know that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: To prevent these predatory tactics, companies would face fines of up to $1,000 for each violation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But to protect small businesses, we're allowing them to avoid being fined if they take immediate corrective action to fix a violation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And of course, New Yorkers can still benefit from legitimate and transparent discounts, whether it be loyalty programs, holiday discounts, or deals for veterans, students, or seniors, just to name a few.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill gives consumers more faith in the system, makes transactions more transparent, and deters corporations from using surveillance pricing to drive up costs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And in working with our state partners, we're laying a foundation to guarantee the highest level of protection for our consumers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And this is building on ways in which the city council is standing up for working New Yorkers and adding to the.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: many steps the council is taking to make the city more affordable for all.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin supports Council Member Farrah Lewis's bill requiring HPD to analyze vacant rent-stabilized units and plan to return them to market.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon highlights Council Member Lewis's vacant rent-stabilized units bill

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Before I turn to the rest of our stated agenda, I also want to acknowledge a bill that Councilmember Farrah Lewis is introducing today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: In the midst of an affordable housing crisis, it's unconscionable that over 50,000 rent-stabilized units

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: are sitting vacant and off the market right here in New York City while so many New Yorkers are struggling to find an affordable place to live.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Councilmember Lewis's legislation works to rectify that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It would require HPD to conduct an analysis of the city's stock of rent-stabilized units and develop a plan to ensure that those units

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: return to the market.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's crucial to our efforts to address the housing shortage because it will finally help ensure more New Yorkers can secure affordable housing that should already be available to them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So thank you, Councilmember Lewis.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin recognizes Veterans Day, thanks colleagues who marched, announces a celebration for veterans, and promotes the bill giving 100% disabled veterans a full property tax exemption.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon honors veterans and announces 100% disabled veteran property tax exemption

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday, we celebrated Veterans Day, and thank you to the colleagues who marched with me in the Veterans Day parade.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Saluting the brave men and women, past and present, who put their lives on the line to serve our country.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And our city honored the approximately 200,000 veterans who live right here in the five boroughs, whose selfless sacrifice we can thank for our safety and our freedom.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're going to be hosting a celebration for them in the chambers next Monday at 530.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: All of our city's veterans are welcome to join us.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: You can RSVP.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: on the council's website, and I hope many of the colleagues can join.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This year, for Veterans Day, we also wanted to put tangible action behind our gratitude.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Because for some of our veterans, their patriotic bravery came at an immense personal cost.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Indeed, thousands of veterans in our city have a serious, permanent, service-related disability.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The least we can do for them who sacrificed their health and their bodies to ensure that they can afford to stay in their homes, to live in the city and the country that they fought hard to defend.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we're voting on a bill that means if you are one of the thousands of veterans with a 100% service disability rating, you pay zero property tax on your home.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I want to thank Councilmember Marano for that bill.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I also want to recognize additional efforts of my colleagues to address other issues facing our veterans, and we have several other bills in our Veterans Day package.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin acknowledges El Dia de los Muertos and Diwali, honoring the festivals' cultural and spiritual significance.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon recognizes El Dia de los Muertos and Diwali

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Moving on to other celebrations, on November 1st and 2nd, it was El Dia de los Muertos, a holiday to honor the spirits of deceased loved ones who temporarily return to the physical world for the day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This past Sunday marked the start of Diwali, the Festival of Lights, celebrated by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and Buddhists.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It honors the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I hope everyone who celebrated enjoyed a meaningful five days.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin recognizes Puerto Rican Heritage Month and the contributions of Puerto Rican communities across the city.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon celebrates Puerto Rican Heritage Month

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: November is poor.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Puerto Rican Heritage Month.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thanks, Elsie.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: From El Barrio to Loizada to the South Bronx, Puerto Rican presence and contributions are felt everywhere and appreciated every single day.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin notes Native American Heritage Month and the over 100,000 Native community members living in New York City.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon recognizes Native American Heritage Month

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: November is also Native American Heritage Month.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: There are over 100,000 enrolled members of Native communities currently living in our city, and we will continue to celebrate their history, present, and future here.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin raises awareness for National Diabetes Month, cites the citywide diabetes reduction plan, and wishes Council Member Shulman a happy belated birthday.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon marks National Diabetes Month and Shulman's birthday

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: November is also National Diabetes Month, raising awareness of the medical condition that affects more than 1 in 10 New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: In 2023, we passed Councilmember Shulman's bill to establish a citywide diabetes reduction plan to ensure that all diabetic residents can access the care that they need.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Speaking of Councilmember Shulman, I want to wish her a happy belated birthday.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin welcomes student journalists brought by Majority Leader Abreu, mentions their mock press conference, and encourages their reporting.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon welcomes student journalists from Urban Assembly Maker Academy

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we have some visitors with us today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Majority Leader Abreu has brought student journalists from the Urban Assembly Maker Academy.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much for joining us.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I hope you enjoyed your mock press conference this morning, and I'm sure that you will be asking us very tough questions in the red room very, very soon.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we can't wait to read your reporting and get literally the inside scoop.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So thank you so much for being here today.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin celebrates Sigma Gamma Rho Day, recognizing the sorority's 1922 founding and 50 sorors in attendance, and thanks Council Member Joseph for the resolution.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon recognizes Sigma Gamma Rho Day

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: November 12th is Sigma Gamma Rho Day in our city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This sorority was founded in 1922 on principles of sisterhood, scholarship, and service, and it's still going strong with 50 sorors here in the audience with us today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We want to thank Councilmember Rita Joseph, who sponsored this resolution for the annual recognition.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And welcome to the People's House.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're so thrilled to have you here.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin thanks Adana Seglecki for 46 years of service as assistant director of human resources, wishing her a happy retirement.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon honors Adana Seglecki on retirement

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And finally, I want to wish congratulations and farewell to a person who has worked for every single speaker of the New York City Council, and that's Adana Seglecki.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Is Donna here today?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, we want to thank Donna.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For her 46 years of service working at the heart of the council as assistant director of human resources.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Donna, thank you so much for everything that you've done, and none of us would be here without you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Any questions that we've had, you always had the answer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're going to miss you here so much, and we wish you a very happy New Year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Very, very happy retirement.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews the South Richmond Designated Open Space Amendment and Studio 54 rehabilitation and text amendment, naming the affected Council districts.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews land use items: South Richmond and Studio 54

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And now we're going to move on to our stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: First, we'll vote on the following land use items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: South Richmond Designated Open Space Amendment will correct longstanding mapping and record-keeping errors and better align the district boundaries with the goals of the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: South Richmond Zoning Relief Plan adopted in November 2023 in Councilmember Frank Marano's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Studio 54 Rehabilitation and Text Amendment will facilitate the preservation of the iconic Studio 54 Theater

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: by allowing more flexibility for the sale of development rights within the theater sub-district and Councilmember Carl Wilson's district.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin notes four preconsidered resolutions sponsored by Council Member Linda Lee to set the city's real property tax rates for fiscal year 2027.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews finance resolutions for FY2027 property tax rates

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Next, we're going to vote on the following finance items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Four pre-considered resolutions, all sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee, to set the City of New York's real property tax rates for fiscal year 2027

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the State of New York, the real property tax law, and the Charter of the City of New York.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we will also vote on the following pieces of legislation.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Resolution 163A sponsored by Deputy Speaker Williams, designating the fourth week of November as Shangri-La's Week.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Resolution 163A: Shangri-La's Week

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 163A, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Dr.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Nantasha Williams, would designate the fourth week of November as the Shangri-La's Week in the City of New York and celebrate their indelible impact on the music of the 1960s.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And ever.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: ever since. Thank you to Regina Paul.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin describes Intro 178A sponsored by Council Member Epstein, requiring city agencies to provide centralized technical assistance for non-residential-to-housing conversions.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 178A: commercial-to-residential conversions

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Section 178A, sponsored by Councilmember Harvey Epstein, would require the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, the Department of Buildings, and other relevant city agencies

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to provide centralized technical assistance to developers and owners seeking to convert

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: non-residential space into housing via designating a liaison to facilitate interagency communications and respond to inquiries and posting guidance on the city's website.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Austin Malone, William Eck, Dirk Spencer, and Jose Conde.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin explains Intro 202A sponsored by Council Member Gutierrez, requiring DOT to install traffic safety improvements near schools within 120 or 180 days of a traffic study.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 202A: school-zone traffic safety timelines

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 202A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, would require the Department of Transportation to make reasonable efforts to install

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: traffic safety improvements, including stop signs, speed reducers, traffic signals,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and designated school loading zones within 120 days of determining through a traffic study that such improvements are appropriate on streets adjacent to schools or within 180 days for traffic signals

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: subject to certain exceptions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Theodore Miller.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Intro 928A sponsored by Council Member Carr, establishing an LGBTQ+ liaison within the Department of Veterans Services.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 928A: LGBTQ+ liaison at Veterans Services

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 928A, sponsored by Councilmember David Carr, would establish an LGBTQ plus liaison within the Department of Veterans Services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Hannah Cohn and Raina Lee.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin describes Intro 488A sponsored by Council Member Vernikov, requiring annual HPD reporting on veterans applying for and selected for Mitchell-Lama housing.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 488A: veteran preference in Mitchell-Lama reporting

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 488A, sponsored by Councilmember Vernikoff, would require an annual report from the Department of Housing Preservation and Development on the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: number of veterans or their surviving spouses applying for housing in city-run Mitchell-Lama developments and the number of veterans being selected for occupancy to ensure that applicants benefiting from a veteran preference are in fact veterans.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Raina Lee.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Intro 1050A sponsored by Council Member Morano, providing a full property tax exemption for permanently and totally disabled veterans' primary residences.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 1050A: disabled veteran property tax exemption

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 1050A.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Sponsored by Councilmember Frank Marano, would provide the primary residence of any permanently and totally disabled veteran

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: shall be fully exempt from taxation and special district charges, assessments, and special ad valorem levies, provided that such veteran meets all other applicable requirements of Section 458A.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Of the real property tax law.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Nicholas Connell and Raina Lee.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin describes her own Intro 891, prohibiting entities from using personal data and algorithms to set different prices for identical goods or services.
chapters.title: Speaker Menon previews Intro 891: surveillance pricing ban

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And then introduction 891, sponsored by myself, will prohibit any entity or service provider from engaging in surveillance pricing defined as pricing set completely or in part by algorithm that uses personal data

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to offer different prices to different customers for the exact same goods or services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Sarah Swain, Rachel Cordera, Natalie Meltzer, and Sarah Liss.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'll turn it back over to our Majority Leader.

chapters.summary: Abreu thanks Speaker Menin, moves into discussion of general orders, reminds members to direct comments to the Chair, and introduces Council Member Wilson as first speaker.
chapters.title: Majority Leader Abreu opens discussion of general orders

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now move into discussion of general orders.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'd like to remind everyone that in debate, all comments should be directed to the Chair.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We'll begin with Councilmember Carl Wilson, followed by Pierina Sanchez.

chapters.summary: Carl Wilson expresses support for Roundabout Theatre Company's Studio 54 rehabilitation, citing arts jobs, economic activity, and cultural preservation.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson supports Studio 54 rehabilitation land use application

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I'm proud to express my support.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: support today for Roundabout Theatre Company's Studio 54 rehabilitation and their land use application, and I hope my colleagues will join me in supporting this worthy endeavor.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Studio 54 is an iconic part of New York City's cultural history.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Preserving spaces like this is essential to keeping our city's arts and entertainment industry vibrant and accessible for generations to come.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: With the council providing capital investment in and legislative support for the Studio 54 rehabilitation, we provided a model for preserving our unique cultural heritage while securing a flourishing future for the arts and culture in the city.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Theater is more than just entertainment.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: It supports jobs, strengthens our local economy, brings visitors to our neighborhoods, and creates opportunities for audiences and artists from all walks of life.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I thank Roundabout Theatre Company for its continued investment in New York City's arts and cultural landscape, and I look forward to seeing Studio 54 continue to thrive as an important part of the Broadway.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Scene and our city's theatrical future.

chapters.summary: Wilson supports Intro 928 establishing an LGBTQ liaison within the Department of Veterans Services and commends Minority Leader Carr.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson backs Intro 928 LGBTQ liaison at Veterans Services

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And I also want to pivot briefly to voice my support on this Veterans Day week for Intro 0928, which would establish an LGBTQ liaison within the Department of Veterans Services.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I commend the LGBTQA caucus colleague, Minority Leader Carr, for his dedication to addressing the needs of LGBTQ vets.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councillor Marano, followed by Minority Leader Carr.

chapters.summary: Morano argues Intro 1051A would fully eliminate property taxes for permanently and totally disabled veterans, thanks 31 sponsors, and notes bipartisan support.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano urges support for Intro 1051A disabled veteran property tax exemption

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Yesterday was Veterans Day, and politicians all over the city marched.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: marched in parades, gave speeches, issued proclamations, and thanked our veterans for their service.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And that's great.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I did plenty of that myself.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But today, we have a chance to do something that will actually make a difference in their lives, which is not something we get to do every day.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Intro 1051A.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Would completely eliminate property taxes on the primary residences of veterans who are permanently and totally disabled because of their military service.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Not a discount, not a reduction, zero property taxes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: These are men and women who've already paid an extraordinary price for our freedom.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: The least we can do is help make sure they can afford to stay in their homes and stay in this city, not have to move to New Jersey where they already do this, or move to Nassau County where they already do this.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Now, getting to this point has been quite an adventure.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We've got 31 sponsors from all five boroughs, spanning just about every political ideology represented in the council.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as we all know, there are quite a few ideologies represented in this council.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Every single member of the Veterans Committee, Democrats and Republicans alike, signed on.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I want to sincerely thank...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All 30 of my colleagues who joined me, and especially Speaker Menon for putting this bill on today's agenda.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And Speaker Menon, your support and leadership helped make today possible.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as the daughter of

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: of a veteran, I can't say that I'm surprised at the leadership you've demonstrated here.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I've spent weeks calling, texting, chasing down colleagues, and frankly, I'm sure some members signed on just to get me to leave them alone.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But think about what we're accomplishing here.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm a Republican from the South Shore of Staten Island, and I've got colleagues sponsoring this bill who probably disagree with me on 95% of the issues we vote on, and some might think the other 5% are negotiable.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But on this, we found common ground.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and I encourage you to vote yes on Intro 1051A.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Minority to Carr, followed by Councilmember Epstein.

chapters.summary: David Carr praises the veterans legislative package, explains Intro 928's goal to help LGBTQ veterans upgrade discharges, and thanks advocates and staff.
chapters.title: Minority Leader Carr supports LGBTQ liaison and veterans package

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: I want to congratulate all my colleagues who are passing legislation today, in particular Chair Morano, Councilmember Palladino, Councilmember Vernikoff.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: The package of legislation that we're putting forward the day after Veterans Day, thanks to the leadership of our Speaker, Julie Menon, is astonishing.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I think my colleague hit the nail on the head that we have to not just give speeches and give applause to our veterans.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: We have to follow that up with actions and deeds that actually support them.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And we are doing that here today.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: In particular, I just want to talk about my piece of legislation, which would create an LGBT liaison at the Department of Veteran Services.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: As we know, for many decades, individuals who are gay or lesbian or bisexual, people who are not straight, could not serve openly in our armed forces.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thankfully, the repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell provided an avenue for veterans who were dishonorably discharged for no reason but for their sexual orientation to get an other than honorable discharge.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Despite that availability, many in New York City do not avail themselves of that, in large part because they don't know how or don't even know that they can.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Now there'll be someone at DVS whose job it is to reach out to them and to try to help them navigate the bureaucracy of the Department of Defense and to try to get their valor restored as it should be because they served honorably.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And that should be reflected in their record.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: So very happy to support this legislation.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: I want to thank all the advocates in particular.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Brian Ellicott for all that they did to make today possible.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Of course, I want to thank our speaker and everyone in the speaker's team for supporting this particular piece of legislation, all my colleagues, in particular Chair Morano for his leadership at the Veterans Committee,

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: as well as folks on the legislative team, Raina Lee, Hannah Cohn, Andrea Vasquez, Jeff Baker, and Johanna Castro, and on my team, Peter Spencer, Justin Belusi, and Giuseppe Desario.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I encourage all my colleagues to support this legislation.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein, followed by Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: First, I want to congratulate Councilmember Morano and Carr on their important packages.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Obviously, Veterans Day was an important moment, and to do something for thousands of veterans to be able to remain in New York is a critical opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to also thank Speaker Menon on Bill 891A, really this idea about prohibiting surveillance pricing and what we've seen happening across the city.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This idea that I was on, I was with my mom at something, and I checked my Uber app, and she checked hers, and literally we were going to the same place, and it was the $5 difference, literally from the same place to the same place.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein

chapters.summary: Epstein explains Intro 178A would create a city system to facilitate commercial-to-residential conversions, citing low vacancy rates and potential for 17,000 new units.
chapters.title: Council Member Epstein promotes Intro 178A for commercial-to-residential conversions

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And finally, for my bill, 178.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We see that we need housing and we need affordable housing across this great city.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And this bill requires when you're converting from commercial to residential conversions, that there's a structure and system in place that the city puts in to ensure that the developers and landlords can do that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: With a vacancy rate of 1.4% and less than 1% for rent-stabilized units, we need to do this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We know that a third of the building units that are being built are in these commercial to residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: 25% of these conversion units are permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This potentially could bring 17,000 new units online if we do this conversion right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This bill will help us go along in this direction.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I encourage my colleagues to vote in favor of this bill.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I appreciate the leadership support.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Inna Vernikov explains her bill requiring HPD to report on veterans applying for and selected in Mitchell-Lama housing, sending data to the Department of Veterans Services.
chapters.title: Council Member Vernikov explains Intro 488A veteran preference reporting

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I am thrilled to see my bill, Intro 488, hopefully pass as part of today's Veterans Bill Package.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Introduction 488A requires that the Department of Housing, Preservation, and Development produce a report on the number of veterans or their surviving spouses applying for housing in City Mitchell-Lama developments

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: and the number of veterans being selected for occupancy, creating a clear way to measure progress.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This bill also sends this report to not just the administration and city council, but crucially to the Department of Veteran Services, whose central mission in our city is to connect, mobilize, and empower veterans in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I introduced this bill because too many veterans struggle to find quality housing, and too few know about the resources available to help them.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: The Mitchell-Lama Veteran Preference is a powerful tool for housing veterans and keeping them in our city.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: My legislative director, Troy Olson, an Army veteran and veteran advocate, has personally housed homeless veterans using this preference.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: We've also worked with veterans who have lived in Mitchell-Lama housing.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: They testified to its high quality while noting its shortcomings and lamenting how few veterans know it exists.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This benefit is currently underutilized.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This bill will make an existing government structure work better and reach the people it was meant to serve.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I'd like to thank Speaker Manin, Committee Legislative Analyst Raina Lee, Legislative...

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: policy analyst Monroe Boot, the Department of Veterans Services, and HPD.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you to Veterans Committee Chair Councilman Morano and everyone else who helped bring this bill forward and take this meaningful step toward housing our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: And of course, thank you to the 200,000 veterans living in New York City for your service.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: First, I want to just congratulate Speaker Menon on banning surveillance.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The surveillance ban, I think it's so important to really uplift the fact that these tech companies are getting away with so much more than we are privy to, and it's a great opportunity for New York to lead.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I want to congratulate my new ledge and comms director, who's been here for a month and already passed a bill, Madeline McGillivray.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I want to thank our awesome, awesome parents advocates and our Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez and her district director, Evelyn Cruz, who

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: First and foremost, my deepest condolences to Councilmember Lewis's community and families and the neighbors devastated by yesterday's building collapse.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That was a horrific tragedy, and I know our council stands ready to support you and your constituents as we also need to secure a full public accounting of what occurred.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The disaster underscores a broader imperative as well.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The city must prevent dangerous building conditions before they become catastrophes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: New Yorkers are reeling from a devastating rise in fires this year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Almost 90 people have died this year compared to the same time period last year, which is twice as much as the previous year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: From Sunset Park in Washington Heights to Mott Haven and the West Bronx, families are enduring relentless loss.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Our first responders are heroic once emergencies begin, but prevention requires confronting underlying hazards.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: More than 80% of our buildings in the city are over 50 years old, and consumer products like lithium-ion batteries and aging electrical systems in older buildings pose the most frequent risk to New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That's why I'm introducing, and I hope my colleagues will support, Intro 1174, which would create an online data dashboard of fire emergencies,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: think NYPD's CompStat, but for fires, and Intro 1175, which would direct the Department of Buildings in collaboration with HPD, FDNY, and...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I look forward to hearing both bills on November 20th.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez

chapters.summary: Lynn Schulman introduces Intro 1176 to strengthen health screenings at central booking, ensuring continuity of care before arraignment, with Deputy Speaker Williams as co-prime sponsor.
chapters.title: Council Member Shulman introduces Intro 1176 on pre-arraignment health screenings

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Today I'm proud to introduce an important piece of legislation to help address critical gaps in health care within our correction system.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: When someone enters the criminal justice system, their health needs do not simply go away.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Someone brought into central booking may have chronic medical conditions, be experiencing a behavioral health crisis, or need daily life-saving medication.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Yet our current correction system lacks the comprehensive screening and resources needed to identify and address these health needs before someone is arraigned.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: My legislation, Intro 1176, aims to address this issue by strengthening pre-arrangement health screenings at central booking facilities across the city.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It would establish a two-level screening process, provide access to trained medical professionals, ensure continuity of care, and provide that individuals who need further evaluation or treatment receive it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: At its core, this legislation is about making sure that people who enter the criminal justice system with health care needs do not fall through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to thank my co-prime sponsor, Deputy Speaker Nantasha Williams, for her support and urge my colleagues to sign on to this important legislation.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.
