chapters.summary: Chi Ossé introduces Intro 1168, the Unconscionable Consumer Abuse Prevention Act, to cut rulemaking delays and let DCWP act faster against exploitative business practices.
chapters.title: Council Member Ossé introduces UNCAP Act to streamline consumer protection enforcement

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: President.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Today, I am proud to introduce Introduction 1168, known as the Unconscionable Consumer Abuse Prevention Act, also known as the UNCAP Act.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: In partnership with Mayor Momdani and the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, we are prepared to ensure our consumer protection laws set a national standard.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: The UNCAP Act will cut red tape, reduce bureaucratic barriers, and embolden the city to act faster against unconscionable business practices.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Even as elected officials, we all share the experience of constantly navigating a marathon of fine print.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Unconscionable business practices can mean charges without people's knowledge, the doom loop of endless dead ends with AI chatbots without a human on the other end.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: We were talking about selling people's personal information, one-sided contract changes that let companies sell work to AI companies, liability waivers, tracking your health data, and I can just keep going on and on and on.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: But right now, the Department of Consumer and Worker Protections cannot challenge this conduct without first completing a lengthy rulemaking process.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: My bill will amend the city's consumer protection laws, cutting months of rulemaking requirements so big businesses think twice before screwing over New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Simply put, bureaucracy cannot be the enemy of getting stuff done.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: This is about faster results for the New Yorkers who are the backbone of our economy and breathe life into the greatest city on earth.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: I look forward to passing this bill with the support of the mayor, Commissioner Levine, and Committee Chair Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to co-sponsor this critical piece of legislation to give our city the authority to hold these bills.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: bad guys accountable, and make life much easier for the people we represent.

utterances.speaker: Chi A. Ossé
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Wilson, followed by Brewer.

chapters.summary: Carl Wilson introduces Intros 1180 and 1181, allowing NYCEM and DSS to station agency staff at cooling and warming centers to connect visitors to city services.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson introduces bills to link cooling and warming center visitors to services

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Cooling and warming centers are community touchstones for New Yorkers looking for relief in harsh weather.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Some visitors might come just to get a quick respite from the heat or cold, while others might have more serious issues.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: A landlord who won't address broken utilities, housing insecurity, or a lack of access to adequate health care.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The city is missing an opportunity by not using cooling and warming centers to connect visitors to resources and information they might need.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The two bills I'm introducing today, Intros 1180 and 1181, would have New York City Emergency Management, who oversees cooling centers, and DSS, who oversees warming centers, offer

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: each center the option of hosting an agency staff member who could then link visitors to city services.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: These bills will imbue cooling and warming centers with greater utility and assist those in need, and I hope my colleagues would consider joining me on these two important bills.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilor Brewer, followed by Riley.

chapters.summary: Gale Brewer introduces a bill to assess agency digital communication, Reso 717 for a foster care insurance risk pool, and Reso 716 opposing renaming Penn Station for Trump.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer introduces digital communication assessment, foster care insurance, and Penn Station renaming resolutions

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Just in terms of an intro to talk about AG.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Agency communication technologies.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think we all know that we rely on digital communication these days for services, but there's been no comprehensive assessment of how these systems are being used.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are they effective?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are they accessible to everyone?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And this would have an examination.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: of agency practices.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Number two, a RESO about foster care and insurance.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: RESO 717 would establish a state-backed insurance risk pool.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This is an almanac.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Update reimbursement rates to reflect rising liability insurance costs and create a bridge fund.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: To help voluntary foster care agencies maintain coverage.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: There are over 6,200 children in this situation in the foster care agencies, and the insurance costs, like elsewhere, are over the moon.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Penn Station renaming, Reso 716.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Basically, don't touch it, President.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Trump, he said he wouldn't release the $16 billion in federal funding for the Gateway Tunnel unless we rename Penn Station after him.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And Penn Station has carried its name for a century.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's busy.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's a hub.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And renaming it would create unnecessary confusion and expense without improving service.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So don't do it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's what this resolution says.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Riley, followed by Marano.

chapters.summary: Kevin Riley introduces Intro 1169 for a safe spaces for creators pilot and Reso 730 urging MTA to revitalize vacant subway retail spaces with veteran-owned business priority.
chapters.title: Council Member Riley introduces safe creator spaces pilot and MTA retail revitalization resolution

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Colleagues, today I'm proud to introduce two pieces of legislation focused on a simple principle.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Opportunities should be accessible to every New Yorker.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Our young people are creating, innovating, and building careers through digital media.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: But too often the lack of safe, accessible spaces forces them into environments that put

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: their safety at risk and limit their potential.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Intro 1169 will establish the safe spaces for creators pilot program through the mayor's office of media and entertainment,

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: providing content creators ages 30 and under with free, secure spaces and city facilities to develop their skills, produce content,

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: and transforming their creativity into opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: We shouldn't just celebrate our young people's potential, we should invest in it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: I'm also introducing Reso 730, calling on MTA to revitalize vacant subway retail spaces and newsstands, while prioritizing opportunities for veteran-owned businesses.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Across our subway systems,

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Too many retail spaces sit vacant.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: These are missed opportunities to support small businesses, strengthen economic activity, and create more vibrant, welcome spaces for commuters.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: This resolution is about putting those spaces back to work while furthering our commitment to the men and women who served our country, creating new pathways to entrepreneurship,

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: and economic stability for our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Our public spaces should serve our communities, not sit empty while opportunities pass us by.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support these measures and help us build a city where more New Yorkers have the space and opportunity to succeed.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilman.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilman Marano, followed by Joseph.

chapters.summary: Frank Morano introduces Intro 1166 to close a loophole allowing developers owing unpaid property taxes or water bills to obtain DOB permits, applying the existing $25,000 threshold.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano introduces Intro 1166 to deny permits to tax-delinquent developers

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There's an old saying that you can't get blood from a stone, but apparently in New York City, you can get a building permit from the...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Department of Buildings, even when you owe the city tens of thousands of dollars.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Today, I am introducing Intro 1166 to close that loophole.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Under current law, if a property owner owes the city $25,000 or more in certain fines and penalties, the DOB can deny them a permit for a major construction project.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But here's the kicker.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If you owe $25,000 in unpaid property taxes or water and sewer bills, those debts don't count.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: How does that make any sense?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I've got a developer in my district involved in a very controversial proposed homeless shelter.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That situation has caused me to take a much closer look at how the city deals with developers who are going to make a lot of money.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And frankly, I don't always like what I see.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: My bill applies one simple principle.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Before City Hall gives you permission to build something new, you ought to settle up with City Hall for what you already owe.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We're keeping this existing $25,000 threshold, protecting necessary safety work, and preserving exceptions for people who are disputing their bills or complying with payment plans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: This isn't a Republican or Democratic issue.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It is a taxpayer issue.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Because the homeowner in Tottenville who pays every property tax bill shouldn't be held to a higher standard than a developer building a multi-million dollar project.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I ask my colleagues to join me in supporting Intro 1166 before we ask New Yorkers to pay more.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let's make sure we're collecting what we're already owed.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Joseph, followed by Joanne.

chapters.summary: Rita Joseph honors the 104th Founders Day of Sigma Gamma Rho, recalling its seven founders and the sorority's motto of greater service and progress.
chapters.title: Council Member Joseph celebrates Sigma Gamma Rho Founders Day

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader, Speaker, colleagues, honored guests, and my beloved Soros.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: 104 years ago today, seven young black women at Butler University, all of them educators, look at the nation that had not made room for them yet.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They didn't wait for permission.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They didn't wait for a seat at the table.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They built their own table, and they set it for service.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Those seven women couldn't have imagined this chamber.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They couldn't have pictured a classroom teacher from Brooklyn standing here as a member in the New York City Council.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They planted the seed anyway.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Our motto is greater service and greater promise, greater progress.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It's a promise that we owe to every child in a classroom, every family fighting to keep their neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In their homes in the 40th district.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So to my sorors, our founders, lit the torch, now it's in our hand.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Let's carry it higher.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Let's carry this torch further.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Happy Founders Day.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Zhuang, followed by Hankerson.

chapters.summary: Susan Zhuang reflects on recent tragedies and introduces Intro 1182 to establish a dedicated Department of Emergency Medical Services, citing EMT pay, staffing, and equipment issues.
chapters.title: Council Member Zhuang introduces Intro 1182 for a dedicated Department of Emergency Medical Services

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: The past two weeks have been incredibly difficult for New York City.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We have witnessed one tragedy after another.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Each one has reminded me how fragile the life can be.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: In my district, we lost six beautiful lives in devastating fire.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: As a member of this community,

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This loss has been deeply affected me.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: My heart is with the

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: families who are grieving and everyone, those who live, whose life has been changed by this tragedy.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: But through every tragedy, one thing has remained consistent.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Our first responders show up.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Our firefighters, police officers, and EMS workers

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: run towards emergencies when the others are running away.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: They provide the care, comfort, and sometimes the difference between life and death.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I have seen firsthand how much our communities depend on them, and I believe thanking them is not enough.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We must also give them the resources, protection, and support they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: The EMTs face unequal pay, staff shortage, and outdated equipment.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: They are not just a workforce issue.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: They are a public safety issue.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: So how can we expect this?

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Challenges to be addressed without department dedicated to EMS.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This is why I reintroduced Intro 1182 legislation to establish a dedicated Department of Emergency Medical Services.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Our EMTs deserve dedicated leadership, fair compensation,

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: proper resources, and a reconsideration they earned.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Colleagues, when our community faced the darkness moment,

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Our EMTs show up for us.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Now it's our turn to show up for them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support Intro 1182.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Hankerson, followed by Santos Uoso.

chapters.summary: Ty Hankerson introduces Intro 1163 requiring digital water safety signage at city beaches to warn about rip currents and changing conditions, and announces a Parks Committee hearing on water safety.
chapters.title: Council Member Hankerson introduces Intro 1163 for digital water safety signage at beaches

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Every summer, thousands of New Yorkers head to our beaches to cool off, spend time with families,

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: with family and enjoy our city's waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: But what many people don't realize is that the water can look perfectly calm while dangerous conditions exist beneath the surface.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Rip currents can develop quickly.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Water conditions can change throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: And too often, beachgoers don't know the risk until it is too late.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: That's why I'm proud to introduce Intro 1163, requiring digital water safety signage at New York City beaches.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: These signs will provide beachgoers with timely information about water conditions, rip current risks, and other important safety warnings.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Because when it comes to water safety, information can be the difference between life and death.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: And I want to be clear, this legislation isn't about replacing lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: It's about giving them another tool to keep New Yorkers safe.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: No parent should have to wonder whether the water their child is entering is safe.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: And no New Yorker should have to learn about a dangerous rip current or what to do after they've already entered the ocean.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: As chair of the Committee on Parks and Recreation, I believe our responsibility doesn't end with making our parks and beaches accessible.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: We must.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: also make them safer, which is why I also encourage all of my colleagues here to attend our Parks Committee hearing tomorrow, where we'll be discussing the state of water safety at our city's beaches and pools.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Council Member Santos Suoso, followed by Justin Sanchez and then Tiffany Caban.

chapters.summary: Kayla Santosuosso mourns the murder of Katie Suarez on the promenade, calls for adequate lighting as a safety measure, and notes Katie's organ donation saved four lives.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso calls for promenade lighting after Katie Suarez murder

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I want to take a moment to acknowledge a 28-year-old young woman who was brutally murdered in my district in the last couple of weeks, and that is, of course, Katie Suarez.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: You've probably heard her name on the news.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: She went out jogging.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Around 8 p.m.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: On the promenade that runs along the edge of my district, along the water.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: She did not return home on time, and unfortunately, her father then went out looking for her and discovered her body lying in the promenade.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: It is a horrific tragedy.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I attended the wake yesterday and was able to give my condolences to the family.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: But I feel that there is action that must be taken, and that is to ensure that there is adequate lighting along the promenade, which is something that people in my district have been calling for for decades.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And we have been met with pushback every step of the way.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And I think in this moment, we can acknowledge that we can't always control everything in order to make

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: someplace safer, but that lighting is an easy way to make a place safer.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Lighting is safety.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Lighting makes us feel safer.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And I'm going to be focusing a lot of attention and resources on trying to get lighting along the promenade where so many people like Katie go for an evening run and should have the ability to feel safe while doing so.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I have been moved by recent reports that Katie, as an organ donor, after she passed, saved the lives of four other people by donating her organs.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And I think that in her name, it is only rightful that we continue saving lives in her honor by ensuring that...

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The promenade that she loved to run on is safe for everybody else to run in years to come.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Justin Sanchez, followed by Kavang.

chapters.summary: Justin Sanchez introduces bills on abandoned delivery totes, residential parking permits, a mural artist portal, and returning unclaimed commissary funds, plus a resolution for the South Bronx.
chapters.title: Council Member Justin Sanchez introduces four bills and resolution for the South Bronx

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, I'm proud to introduce four bills and one resolution aimed at addressing a host of issues residents are experiencing in the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Each piece of legislation is part of a multifaceted approach to address quality of life, improve public safety, and expand opportunities for residents to take ownership of their communities.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Reclaiming our streets, holding delivery companies accountable for abandoned totes.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: As last mile delivery companies like Amazon expand their operations across New York City, abandoned delivery totes and plastic bins have become increasingly common on sidewalks, stoops, and in tree pits.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This legislation would authorize the Department of

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: sanitation to remove abandoned delivery totes and charge the responsible shipping company a per container fee.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This bill would protect public spaces, reduce litter, save taxpayers money, and encourage more responsible delivery practices.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Reclaiming our parking, putting Bronx residents first.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: For many South Bronx residents, finding a parking space near their homes has been a daily challenge.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Residential streets are lined with abandoned vehicles and cars with out-of-state plates, many of which are owned by residents looking to evade registration fees.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This legislation would require the Department of Transportation to establish a residential parking permit program in the South and the Southeast Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Reclaiming our public spaces, creating opportunities for local mural artists,

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: With the largest mural in the country unveiled in the South Bronx, I know everyone is asking, what about us?

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This legislation would establish a centralized online portal connecting artists with available opportunities across the five boroughs, making it easier for artists to find projects and for property owners, community organizations, and city agencies to connect with local talent.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Reclaiming our money and our freedom, returning unclaimed commissary funds to formerly incarcerated New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: According to the Department of Correction, approximately 4.3 million in unclaimed commissary funds remains in the agency's possessions, money that rightfully belongs to formerly incarcerated New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Many returning citizens are unaware that this money remains unclaimed or do not know how to retrieve it.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This bill would require the Department of Correction to conduct an outreach campaign notifying formerly incarcerated individuals of the money that is rightfully theirs and how to recover it.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, Councilmember, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Norma Kaban.

chapters.summary: Tiffany Cabán introduces a resolution supporting Starbucks Workers United's boycott, citing five years without a first contract and union-busting tactics.
chapters.title: Council Member Cabán introduces resolution supporting Starbucks Workers United boycott

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: First, I just want to say that, like my colleagues, my heart goes out to our neighbors in Brooklyn who were killed and injured in last night's tragic collapse in Flatbush.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I'm grateful to Councilmember Farrah Lewis's leadership in responding and for all of the city agencies that have mobilized to support the survivors and the families of those who perished.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And just echo my colleague's sentiments that we are all here to support Flatbush in this moment.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And today, I am proud to introduce a resolution supporting the call by Starbucks Workers United for a boycott of Starbucks.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Until the company bargains fairly with its workers.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's been five years since that first Starbucks store voted to unionize, five years and Starbucks still has refused to bargain a first contract with any of its workers, instead relying on age-old union-busting tactics to avoid their responsibility

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: to negotiate fairly.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: This resolution is about a standing with Starbucks baristas and with workers organizing across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: The Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Martin Luther King Jr.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Said that the labor movement is, quote, the principal force that transformed misery and despair into hope and progress.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: That was true last century, and it's true today.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: As we work to hold the oligarchs and fascists like Trump and other billionaires accountable and to build power for the working class in New York and across the country, the labor movement will be the bedrock of that work.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And Philadelphia passed a similar resolution last month, and now it's our turn to join them.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So thank you, and I hope that my colleagues will co-sponsor.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I have one more speaker, Councilmember Altabal.

chapters.summary: Shirley Aldebol introduces Intro 1158 to eliminate non-refundable pet fees and cap monthly pet rent at 1% of rent, citing housing instability as a leading cause of pet surrenders.
chapters.title: Council Member Aldebol introduces Intro 1158 Pet Rent Limit Act

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Today I'm proud to introduce Intro 1158 or the Pet Rent Limit Act.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Across the city, pet rent and fees have grown significantly, putting an increased financial burden on New Yorkers already struggling with rising costs.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Landlords can use pet rent to tack on additional monthly costs to pet owners'leases, creating a barrier for new renters and rehoused people.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Pet rents can also force families already struggling to keep up with the cost of living to make the difficult choice of giving up their pets.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The Pet Rent Limit Act would change New York City's administrative code to eliminate non-refundable upfront charges and fees and cap monthly pet rent at 1% of the agreed rental amount.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: According to ACC data from 2025, one in three pet surrenders in the city are direct result of housing instability.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The increase in animals entering shelters reflects the affordability challenges that many New Yorkers are facing.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: No New Yorker should ever have to give up their beloved pet because they cannot afford housing with them.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: More affordable housing for pet owners can be critical to helping ease the financial burden facing New Yorkers and save them from these impossible choices.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The CAP structure acknowledges the impact that pet ownership can have on building-wide maintenance costs for property owners, managers, and workloads for building staff.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: workers while preventing unreasonable costs to tenants.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The Pet Rent Limit Act will help the city reduce the number of animals that end up in shelters while improving affordable rental options for New Yorkers in need of housing.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I hope my colleagues on the City Council will join me in supporting our city's pet owners and taking this small but impactful step

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: for making our city a more affordable place to live.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein, my apologies for missing you the first time.

chapters.summary: Harvey Epstein introduces Intro 1160 to require delivery app companies to provide indoor spaces for drivers to charge, store bikes, and access facilities.
chapters.title: Council Member Epstein introduces Intro 1160 on delivery app worker spaces

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Really, my heart goes out to the families in Brooklyn, and thank you, Councilmember Lewis, for her leadership on this, and try to, as Councilman Perina Sanchez said before, think about how we can not have these continue to happen in New York.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to flag for my colleagues that intro 1160, which I introduced today and focused on to ensure that

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: when delivery apps are working in New York City, that they have locations for delivery drivers to be.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: What we see in New York City is delivery drivers are just on the streets of New York, parking their bikes overnight, have no place to store them, and that impacts the neighborhood where they're in.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And the app companies who are sending people on the streets have no responsibility to ensure they have indoor spaces to charge.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: They have no responsibility to ensure people have lunch, to go to the bathroom, you know, indoor space to keep their bikes overnight.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: That becomes dangerous for the riders and difficult for communities.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This bill will require and hold the app companies responsible to ensure when these

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: things are happening, they are held accountable to make sure there's a place and opportunity for those workers.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This protects the workers, protects communities, and ensures app companies have the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I encourage my colleagues to look at this bill.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I hope for a quick conversation about how important this bill is.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Council holds its November 12, 2026 stated meeting, opening with an invocation by Chaplain Patrick Lime and a roll call.
Speaker Julie Menin delivers a wide-ranging communication covering the Flatbush building collapse, Flight 587 anniversary, Veterans Day, the surveillance pricing ban, and previews the agenda.
The Council adopts land use call-ups, general orders with several split votes, and voice votes on resolutions, followed by member introductions of new bills and adjournment.
